answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The basalt multiplier is published, charged in inlet, and reef lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2159 identities would post 2128 proofs and burn roughly 76 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
